sections.h2: Three offices behind a Fayette County bill
sections.html:
Three offices share the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's value. The Sheriff takes the current year's payment. Bills that run late go to the County Clerk. Lexington and Fayette County merged governments on January 1, 1974, so there is no separate city bill. One statement covers every taxing district.

The PVA works from 101 East Vine Street, Suite 600, in Lexington (phone 859-246-2722, fax 859-246-2729). The PVA neither sets rates nor accepts payments. The sheriff's Property Tax Division is in Room 236 of the Fayette District Courthouse at 150 North Limestone, reachable at 859-252-1771. Counter hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, with closing pushed to 6:00 p.m. during October. The office collects over 110,000 bills worth nearly $260 million a year.

The bill pays for the Commonwealth, Fayette County Public Schools, the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, called LFUCG here, the county extension and soil conservation districts, the health department, Lextran and a park fund. Property in the Downtown Lexington Management District carries a further charge.

Take the assessed value, subtract any exemption, and multiply by the rate for the property's tax district, per $100 of value. Values are fixed each January 1 at fair cash value, meaning what the parcel would most probably sell for on the open market.

Rates depend on which city services a parcel receives. The seven residential districts share the same state, school, general services, extension, conservation, health, Lextran and park fund lines. They differ only in refuse, street light, street cleaning or full-service charges.

Real property rates in Fayette County for 2026, in dollars per $100 of assessed value

1Full services1.2598

3Refuse1.2238

Properties certified as abandoned and blighted by the LFUCG Vacant Property Review Commission pay an extra $1 per $100. Downtown Lexington Management District parcels pay an extra $0.10 per $100.

Bills are payable through December, with a discount for paying early. Statements are mailed in the last week of September. If you have no bill by about October 10, call 859-252-1771 for a duplicate, since a missing bill is no excuse for nonpayment.

  • October 1 to November 1: pay the face amount less 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: full face amount, no discount.
  • January 1 to January 31: 5 percent penalty.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 10 percent penalty with a further 10 percent add-on.
  • After April 15: delinquent at 21 percent and handed to the County Clerk.

You can pay at the sheriff's counter (cash, check or money order), at any Lexington Republic Bank lobby through January 31 with the bill coupon, on the online portal (card or bank debit, with a convenience fee the sheriff does not receive) or by mail to PO Box 34148, Lexington, KY 40588-4148. A mailed payment counts at the amount due on its postmark date, and a postage meter stamp is not accepted as proof. The sheriff cannot take installments or grant extensions, and a returned check adds a $35 fee.

Speak with a PVA assessor first, and only afterward take an appeal to the County Clerk. The PVA reviews each of its roughly 300 assessment areas every three to four years under a state quadrennial plan, and neighborhood sales drive most reassessments. Many owners receive a notice in April that includes a map of recent sales close to the property.

The PVA conference and the clerk's appeal to the Local Board of Tax Appeals both fall in May. Kentucky's calendar places the tax roll inspection across the 13 days that start on the first Monday of May, so the window recurs yearly. Postmarks do not count for the appeal form, so deliver it to the clerk.

  • Bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal, photographs, insurance policies, construction costs, listings or sale contracts.
  • A paid representative must attach a letter of authorization from the owner.
  • Hearings take place at the LFUCG Phoenix Building, 101 East Vine Street, in a first-floor conference room, and the clerk mails each appellant a time.
  • After the roll is finalized, the PVA still accepts a request for review, though it cannot change the bill already issued for that year.

For the clerk's appeals desk, dial 859-253-3344.

A qualifying home loses $49,100 of assessed value under the exemption, a figure the state set for 2025 and 2026. An owner qualifies by turning 65 at any point in the calendar year or by being classed as totally disabled. It only applies to your primary residence.

The disability route needs total disability status under a public or private retirement system, payments across the calendar year, and a yearly confirmation to the PVA. A copy of the system's disability letter serves as proof. For age, a driver's license, birth certificate or registration, passport, school record or marriage record will do.

Each residence gets one exemption and each person gets one. Send applications by mail to the Fayette PVA at 101 East Vine Street, Suite 600, by fax to 859-246-2729 or by scan to the PVA's email.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or due
sections.html:
Ownership on January 1 decides who is billed, so a seller may receive a statement for a year in which the buyer takes title. After a sale, the PVA tries to mail the bill in care of the new owner, though a closing near printing time can outrun the update. Take questions about the prorated share to the closing agent or attorney. The sheriff does not issue prorated bills or accept prorated payments.

Anything unpaid after April 15 lands at the County Clerk. Payment there must be cash, a money order, or a cashier's or certified check made out to the Fayette County Clerk. Partial payments are refused and interest accrues monthly. Owners who cannot pay in full can call the County Attorney's Office at 859-254-4941 about an arrangement.

Each summer the clerk offers eligible delinquent bills to third-party buyers, some time between day 90 and day 135 after the handover. Clerk and attorney charges pile on top of the penalties. A sale ordered by a court, including for delinquent taxes, goes through the Master Commissioner. The clerk also runs a free alert service that emails you when a filing is recorded under a name or address you register.

sections.h2: Housing and selling in Fayette County
sections.html:
Fayette County is a 286 square mile urban county in the central Bluegrass region, with Lexington as its seat and only city. Population is 329,751. There are 152,488 housing units, and 53.8 percent are owner-occupied. Median home value for owners is $293,500, and median gross rent is $1,164.

Nearly half of homes are rented, so a house needing work or carrying a tax balance can still find buyers. When a sale must close fast and without repairs, a buyer paying cash for the house as it stands can settle the tax out of the proceeds. Get a payoff figure from the sheriff first so the title company knows what to hold back.

faqs.q: When is the 2% discount deadline in Fayette County?
faqs.a: The discount ends on November 1 of the assessment year. It runs from October 1 and cuts the bill by 2 percent. After that, the full amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Fayette County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Sheriff's Property Tax Division in Room 236 of the Fayette District Courthouse, 150 North Limestone, with cash, a check or a money order. Any Lexington Republic Bank lobby also takes payments through January 31 if you bring the bill coupon.

faqs.q: What is the Fayette County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 of value from a qualifying primary residence. The owner has to turn 65 during the calendar year or be totally disabled, and the PVA at 859-246-2722 processes applications.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Fayette County assessment after the window closes?
faqs.a: Not for the current bill. The PVA conference and the clerk's appeal filing both fall inside the May inspection period. After that you can still request a review through the PVA, but a finalized assessment cannot change the bill for that year.

faqs.q: What if Fayette County taxes stay unpaid?
faqs.a: If still unpaid on April 15, the bill goes delinquent at 21 percent and transfers to the County Clerk, which adds monthly interest and fees. The clerk may then sell the bill to an outside buyer at the summer sale.
